title: Angular leaf spot on common bean

Header: Angular leaf spot on common bean
Pseudocercospora griseola ( Phaeoisariopsis griseola ) Chichewa: Madontho-madontho a nyemba

Prevention: Pathogen is seed borne so use certified disease-free seed.
Removal of crop debris or residues from the field to avoid them acting as source of inoculum.
Deep ploughing of crop residues to reduce inoculum.
Avoid moving in the field when the plants are wet to avoid spreading the disease.
Crop rotation with non-host crop e.g. maize, potato and cassava for at least 2 years.
Remove bean volunteer plants in the field.
Monitoring: Monitor during late flowering and early pod formation period.
Check for symptoms of angular leaf spot on leaves, stems, pods and seeds.
On leaves look for spots that are confined between veins and have angular appearance.
Lesions grey in colour and later turn into light brown.
On pods look for large, oval or circular, reddish brown spots usually surrounded by a darker margin.
Look for elongated dark brown lesion on stem, petion and branches.
Take action when 5% of plants are infected.
Direct Control: Uproot and bury heavily infected plants to prevent further disease spreading.
SC (Colloso) at the rate of 80ml per 20 litres of water.
Chlorothalonil 720g/L (Bravo 720SC, Rova 720SC, Daconil) at a rate of 1.4-2.3
EW) at the rate of 20ml/15 litres of water.
Restrictions: Use personal protective equipment when handling and applying pesticides.
Do not eat, drink or smoke when mixing or applying pesticides.
